record.original_question: If the points of the plane are colored with n colors, must there exist a color c such that for every distance d > 0 there are two points A and B of color c, with the segment AB also monochromatic in color c, and with distance AB = d? The same question is intended for space as well.

evidence.quote: Conjecture: No matter how the points of a plane are colored with n colors, there exists a color which fulfills all distances ... (The result would implicitly be true in space, too.)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 2$ be a fixed integer. Suppose every point of the Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ is assigned one of $n$ colors (i.e., a function $\chi : \mathbb{R}^2 \to \{1,2,\dots,n\}$ is given, with no measurability or regularity assumption). Say that a color $c \in \{1,\dots,n\}$ "fulfills the distance $d > 0$ in the strong sense" if there exist two points $A, B \in \mathbb{R}^2$ with $\chi(A) = \chi(B) = c$, with $|AB| = d$, and such that every point of the closed line segment $\overline{AB}$ also has color $c$ under $\chi$.

Prove or disprove: for every $n$-coloring $\chi$ of $\mathbb{R}^2$ there exists at least one color $c$ that fulfills every distance $d > 0$ in the strong sense, i.e., for every $d > 0$ one can find such a monochromatic segment of length $d$ entirely in color $c$.

Settle the analogous statement for $n$-colorings of three-dimensional Euclidean space $\mathbb{R}^3$, where again one asks whether some color class must contain, for every $d > 0$, a closed segment of length $d$ all of whose points carry that color.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches on Euclidean Ramsey theory and colorings of the plane (Hadwiger–Nelson, odd-distance graphs, Davies's recent results on odd and polynomial/prime monochromatic distances) reveal active progress on which distances must be monochromatically realized in finite colorings of the plane, but no source was found that directly resolves the stronger statement requiring an entire segment (not merely its endpoints) of every prescribed length to be monochromatic in a single color class. The status of this specific strengthened conjecture, in both the plane and 3-space, could not be verified from available sources.

status_evidence.title: Odd Distances in Colourings of the Plane (James Davies)
status_evidence.snippet: Every finite colouring of the plane contains a monochromatic pair of points at an odd distance.
status_evidence.claim: Recent progress addresses monochromatic pairs at prescribed distances, but considers only endpoints, not whole segments.

status_evidence.title: Prime and polynomial distances in colourings of the plane
status_evidence.snippet: For every finite colouring of the plane, there is a monochromatic pair of points whose distance is prime; similar results for polynomial values.
status_evidence.claim: Current Euclidean Ramsey results concern monochromatic point pairs at specified distances, leaving the stronger 'monochromatic segment' version unresolved in the literature found.

status_evidence.title: Hadwiger–Nelson problem
status_evidence.snippet: Standard reference for chromatic number of the plane.
status_evidence.claim: Background problem; does not address the specific strong-segment conjecture.
